articleTitle: Digitalizing Unorganised Labour Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: In the labor landscape of 2024, today's workers encounter issues such as delayed payments, difficulty finding nearby job opportunities, limited access to insurance, and in-adequate knowledge of labor laws and schemes. In response, our innovative web platform is designed to provide comprehensive solutions. The platform allows laborers to easily locate nearby job opportunities by specifying their work preferences and their pincode. Each laborer will receive a unique identification number during registration. It is accessible in multiple regional languages to accommodate a diverse user base. Additionally, the website introduces a labor agency feature, empowering group supervisors to efficiently allocate tasks, manage payments from employers, and equitably distribute earnings to workers. A robust two-way authentication system ensures payment transparency and eliminates disputes. Payments are made in cash, with a secure OTP verification process to safeguard transactions. Daily attendance records are managed through UIN codes. The platform also offers access to labor insurance options, purchasable by employers or workers based on their needs. This system can be implemented using React JS for the frontend and MongoDB as the database. This marks a pivotal step in India's labor sector digital transformation, promising enhanced worker welfare and a more efficient labor ecosystem.

articleTitle: IOT Based Smart Parking System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: More students and faculty members coming to the college by their own vehicles leading to parking issues. The parking challenges faced by faculty members at institute due to crowded parking spaces and a high number of vehicles, is one of the major concern for the management. This presents an IoT-based smart parking system leveraging Arduino Uno microcontroller technology. The designed model utilizes infrared sensors at each parking spot to notice the occurrence of vehicles and provide real-time updates on parking availability. The sensors interface with the Arduino Uno, which processes the data and displays available spaces on LCD screens within the parking area. A servo motor controlled gate, managed by the Arduino, regulates vehicle entry and exit based on real-time parking data. This proposed model optimizes parking efficiency, streamlines vehicle movement and dynamically adapts to changing conditions, thereby enhancing parking management. In future this model may provide in advance about the parking details via mobile notifications for faculty member so that they can plan in advance to park their vehicle.

articleTitle: Coffee Plant Disease Identification Using Quantum Fourier Transform Image Processing and EfficientNetV2-S
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Indian Coffee is known worldwide for its aroma and quality. Meeting the quality also the the international market export demand for Coffee is challenging due to various issues like environmental conditions, biotic stress, etc. The proposed work considered the biotic stress of Coffee plants namely Cescospora, Rust, Miner, and Phoma which are critical in meeting the expected outcome from coffee farms. In different aspect, the real-time collection of data is a crucial task. Hence the work developed a QFT image processing for the diseased images and evaluated the results by the EfficientNetV2-S model. The recommended system achieved of accuracy 95.60%, 98.78%,98.5%,96.20, and 99.17% respectively for Cescospora, Rust, Miner, Phoma, and, Healthy.

articleTitle: YouTube Viralomics: A Scoring Framework by Analyzing Engagement Metrics in the Indian Context
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: In today's digital landscape, understanding the dynamics of virality in online video content has become crucial due to its impact on brand visibility, audience engagement, and social influence. For content creators and marketers, understanding and quantifying virality will enable them to tailor their strategies effectively. This research focuses on developing a unique framework termed “viralomics” to measure virality by using a dataset of ten thousand trending YouTube videos of Indian content creators. Sophisticated usage of statistical techniques are employed for data analysis and feature elimination to identify the most impactful features. Further, Regression analysis and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) are used to find the ideal weights for these shortlisted features. The resulting equation for the virality score achieves an impressive R square (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) value of 0.913 and a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0020. The model was further validated using a two-step validation process, consisting of a validation dataset and case studies.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: From Monolith to Microservices: A Systematic Literature Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Microservices are an architectural approach that decomposes applications into small, independently deployable services, enhancing scalability and agility. The application of microservices architecture in numerous enterprises, aimed at modernizing their existing applications, emerges as a noteworthy trend. Despite the extensive research conducted on migration processes, there is a noticeable lack in understanding the essential principles necessary for the efficient implementation of microservices architecture. This study seeks to consolidate the comprehension of the fundamental concepts inherent in the object-oriented approach and their importance in both monolithic and microservices architectures. Moreover, an analysis of the design patterns and principles utilized in microservices, along with comparisons to monolithic architectures, is undertaken. The investigation delves into the advantages and disadvantages of monolithic and microservices architectures, offering valuable insights for scholars and practitioners in the field.

articleTitle: Intent Dataset Creation for Indian Tourism Based Chatbot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: In recent years, the development of intelligent chatbots and generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) models has revolutionized the way users interact with digital systems, particularly in the domain of tourism. There is, however, a severe lack of data available for Indian tourism to train chatbots. This study proposes a new dataset specifically designed for classifying requests related to Indian tourism based on their purpose. For generative AI, intent categorization is essential for correctly defining the intention of a query and giving an appropriate answer. It aims at offering precise, contextualized interactions while avoiding ambiguous responses in order to enhance customer contentment. The dataset addresses various user intents including inquiries for information, reservations, planning activities and recommendations among others. The intents are split into 19 distinct types. With this dataset, chatbot systems will be able to understand and respond more accurately to user inquiries, thereby improving user experience. The paper provides a detailed discussion about how this was achieved, how the dataset is structured and its potential applications in the development of tourismrelated chatbots.

articleTitle: Investigating the Efficacy of Forensic Facial Reconstructions: A Dual Approach Using Sketches and CCTV Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: The evolution of forensic facial recognition has driven the development of a groundbreaking two-model system engineered to identify suspects by digitally removing facial obstructions such as masks and glasses. Throughout history, CCTV captures and forensic sketches have been pivotal in criminal investigations, yet their efficacy has been limited by challenges like low resolution and poor lighting conditions. This innovative system harnesses Generative Adversarial Networks GAN to elevate inputs from CCTV captures and forensic sketches. Model A excels at transforming forensic sketches into realistic images, refining resolution and color fidelity to enhance accuracy in suspect identification. Model B integrates GFP-GAN, pix2pix GAN, and StyleGAN to effectively eliminate facial obstructions, thereby refining outputs for heightened realism. Leveraging advanced image processing techniques, including convolutional neural networks and transfer learning, Model B adeptly handles diverse and challenging conditions. Methodologically, the system involves meticulous dataset collection, rigorous training, and precise processing utilizing the CelebAMask-HQ dataset for Model A, and seamless integration of GFP-GAN, pix2pix GAN, and StyleGAN for Model B. Demonstrated results underscore the system's prowess in processing varied inputs and bolstering facial recognition accuracy, pivotal for applications in law enforcement and national security. Authorities benefit from expedited identification processes, facilitating swift suspect tracking and crime prevention. Looking ahead, ongoing advancements aim to integrate Neural Radiance Fields into the GAN framework, promising enhanced visual fidelity and enabling real-time suspect identification. This continuous evolution marks a paradigm shift in forensic facial recognition capabilities, empowering law enforcement agencies worldwide with robust tools for effective crime mitigation.

articleTitle: Low Power Line Product Code for Reliable Memories
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: This world is working mostly with wireless network systems, which has made data communication more sophisticated and securing the data plays a vital role. Due to this, Error Correction Codes (ECCs) have had huge demand in the real world. This paper focuses on the Low Power Line Product Code (LPC) which is an extension of the Modified Extended Hamming Error Correction Code and includes redundant bits like parity and extended parity bits in columns and rows. The LPC is a new solution of ECC which is designed with an increased error correction rate. The LPC is modified by introducing a novelty idea to decrease the number of parity bits to attain the same error correction rate. The novelty approach has given optimized and efficient results, resulting in a low-power LPC. The result is optimized with the area by a percentage of 4.66% and the total power by a percentage of 38.63%. This design is designed and verified at 90nm technology using the Cadence tool.

articleTitle: Improving Fake News Detection on Social Media Platforms Using Modified Metaheuristics and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Social networking and emerging technologies have fundamentally reshaped personal connectivity online. Despite the increasing reliance on the internet for everyday tasks, entertainment, and community building by businesses, corporations, and individuals, online social interactions continue to pose challenges. Misuse of social platforms can lead to the spread of misinformation. This issue has brought the emergence of fake news to the forefront of societal concerns. The vast volumes of data and rapidly evolving language used on social media platforms render traditional approaches, like static filter lists, ineffective. This study proposes a data-driven approach leveraging applied AI to detect and mitigate online misinformation using advanced natural language processing (NLP) techniques. A modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is introduced for hyperparameter optimization, demonstrating promising results in maximizing performance. A comparative analysis across several contemporary optimizers on a real-world dataset demonstrates the efficacy of the proposed approach, achieving an accuracy of 0.846620 with the best-optimized models.

articleTitle: Field Monitoring and Insect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: In agriculture, the identification and categorization of pests at an early stage is a necessity to procure crop protection and maximum output. Early detection and categorization of pests in the modern-day scenario is of much essence in capturing high crop protection and outputs. Traditional means of monitoring for detection of pests include manual surveillance, and obviously, it is a very tedious work process and prone to flaws. In an innovative approach, this paper suggests a novel system called the Internet of Things-Driven Field Monitoring and Insect Classification System. Such a proposed system uses infrared sensors, a sound sensor, capacitive touch sensors, motion sensor to detect the presence of targeted pests like Melanoplus Sanguinipes In such a way, such sensors capture multidimensional ambient information: about the sounds it makes, motion, and the touch, so that the conditions of the field may be monitored in real-time. In sound sensors feature values of insect and other noise sounds are taken joining them together, annotating them, and training a logistic regression model with this data can classify the sounds. Data taken in by sensors are wirelessly transferred to the Blynk platform through NodeMCU access for the agriculture stakeholders.

articleTitle: Leveraging Amazon Web Services IoT for Predictive Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) is a condition based maintenance strategy that leverages real-time data from sensors and machine learning algorithms to identify potential equipment failures before they occur. This approach enables proactive maintenance scheduling, reducing unplanned downtime and extending equipment lifespan. The Internet of Things (IoT) plays a crucial role in PdM by providing real-time data on equipment performance and health. IoT sensors embedded in machines collect data on various parameters, which is then analyzed using machine learning algorithms to detect anomalies and patterns indicative of potential failures. By integrating IoT data with maintenance management systems, organizations can optimize maintenance schedules, reduce costs, and improve overall equipment effectiveness (OEE). This paper provides a comprehensive overview of predictive maintenance, its benefits, and the role of IoT in enabling proactive maintenance strategies.

articleTitle: Data-Set for Normal and Suspicious Behavior in ATM Booths
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: This research paper presents a Data Set for an innovative neural networking model designed to enhance the security of Automated Teller Machines (ATM) through the detection of suspicious activities in real-time video streams. The proposed model utilizes advanced computer vision techniques and deep learning methodologies to analyze video feeds from ATM cameras. By identifying unusual behaviors such as bending down and looking away from the screen, the system aims to provide robust intrusion detection capabilities, thereby preventing potential fraudulent activities. The model's effectiveness is evaluated through extensive experimentation, demonstrating its potential to enhance the security landscape of ATM operations significantly.

articleTitle: Unified Framework for Classical Music Generation Using GANs, VAEs, and Diffusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: This paper presents a framework to create new music using generative deep learning. Specifically, to create Western classical piano music based on music from Bach, Schubert, Chopin, and other famous composers. The core idea introduced is to use advanced Variational Autoencoders (VAE), Diffusion Models, and Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) and combine them to create a better-performing model capable of generating classical piano music finetuned to the specific composers. The proposed ensemble methodology involves initial separate pretraining of a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) and a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) on the dataset. Subsequently, the VAE encoder is utilized to establish a latent space, which undergoes refinement via a Diffusion Model. This refined latent space is then employed by the generator component, previously trained within the GAN framework, to generate novel music compositions adhering to the stylistic characteristics associated with specific music composers.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Deep Architecture for Bharatanatyam Face Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: This paper explores deep learning techniques for classifying facial emotions in the traditional South Indian Bharatanatyam dance. The model determines the performance of several pre-trained fashions with a dataset on a dataset specifically for this cause. There are Densenet-201, Densenet-121, Densenet-161, Resnext-101_32×8d, Inception-V3, Wideresnet101-2, and VGG-16 are all a few of the fashions considered as properly. Regnety-32GF, Efficientnet-b6, Regnety-800MF, and Efficientnet-b7 are also among the models considered. Initially, the performance metrics for each model, including accuracy, precision, and F1-score, are referred to. After that, K-fold validation was used to assess the pre-trained models’ generalization and stability. Regnety-32GF performance is higher than the alternative models, as confirmed by its finest accuracy of 99.40% using K-fold validation. The observation highlights the significance of using advanced techniques that include K-fold validation to ensure dependable version performance.

articleTitle: Automated Web Scraping for Telecom Corpus Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: The necessity for effective techniques of data collection and analysis has grown as the amount of data available on the internet has increased. One technique that enables us to take information from websites and save it for later examination is web scraping. By creating a tool that can gather pertinent information from telecom websites and store it in a structured fashion for analysis, we hope to automate the process of web scraping for telecom corpus as part of this project. Python is the programming language that we employ, along with several packages for web scraping, including Beautiful Soup and Selenium. This paper seeks to provide insights into the methodology of creating a web application that a certain user could use to scrape telecom websites.

articleTitle: Chat GPT and Cyber Risks: Need of Custom Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Due to growing utilization of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for small, medium, and large business organizations cybersecurity risks are increasing. While AI provides enormous opportunities to generate great insight, it also enables risks on data privacy or network security. Organizations are integrating Chat GPT to enhance customer experience by providing personalization, product recommendations, and immediate responses of users’ queries. However, if underline AI models have not been trained appropriately or default ready to use models have been used to generate responses, the cybersecurity risk will be increased. The paper will discuss about the prompt injection attack in which an attacker can exploit the vulnerabilities of large language models (LLM) to get sensitive data or system specific information to incorporate data breach or other cyber-attacks. The study compares the response of cybersecurity related questions for Chat GPT and Ollama LLM models to discuss the possible cyber risks and suggest the need of custom LLM models for organizations. The paper also provides an approach how these risks can be quantified using concept of Cyber Value at Risk (CVaR).

articleTitle: Interpretation of Remote Sensing Images Using Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Over the decades, with the massive advancements in the technology industry, the interpretation of remote sensing satellite images has also adopted machine learning methodologies. However, these are still traditional interpretation methods that face heavy challenges due to limited contextual understanding and the inability to interpret images covering vast areas. Our proposed methodology for addressing this involves leveraging OpenStreetMap(OSM) data to build comprehensive knowledge graphs. Extracting crucial features like polygons from Remote Sensing (RS) images, using the Segment Anything Model(SAM), will enable us to query these graphs and hence provide us with the essential contextual interpretation of low-resolution satellite images, in particular. This novel approach provides us with the essential attributes of efficiency and scalability.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Smart Pharmacy Systems: A Comprehensive Implementation Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: The fast-paced advancements in Internet of Things (IoT) technology offer transformative possibilities for healthcare systems, particularly in managing and dispensing medications. Based on real-time input parameters, this research paper explores the growth and execution of a Smart Pharmacy System (SPS) designed to automate the dispensing of medicines. Robot technology has helped to leverage Industry Revolution 4.0 all over the world. We explore the design and implementation of a robotic arm-based smart pharmacy system that leverages advanced technologies to automate the precise dispensing of medications. By integrating microcontrollers, IoT sensors, and sophisticated software algorithms, the system processes electronic prescriptions to accurately identify, measure, and dispense the correct dosages of medications. The robotic arm, equipped with precise grippers and verification mechanisms, ensures the right medication is selected and prepared for patients, significantly reducing human error and enhancing safety. This approach not only streamlines the dispensing process, improving efficiency in busy healthcare environments but also offers robust inventory management and real-time data tracking.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Enabled Facial Recognition Using Siamese Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Facial recognition technology has become increasingly vital in various applications, from security systems to personalized user experiences. By using a Siamese network, a kind of deep learning model intended to examine and identify similarities between input images, this study aims to increase the accuracy of facial recognition. Through the use of a Siamese network and a contrastive loss function, the system is able to discriminate between pairs of facial photos that are similar and those that are not. The methodology includes extensive testing to assess the network's performance once it has been trained on varying amounts of data. The paper aims to provide a robust and scalable facial recognition solution with potential applications in security, authentication, and user personalization systems.

articleTitle: Graph-Theoretic Measures for Supporting Diagnosis and Identification of Biomarkers for Borderline Personality Disorder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) is a mental health disorder which renders an individual a victim of severe mood swings, impulsive behaviour, self-destructive behaviour and a distorted self-image. The diagnosis of BPD is usually conducted based on subjective assessments. However with the growing developments in neuroimaging, computational techniques can be developed leading to faster and more accurate diagnosis. In our study, we utilize neuroimaging techniques, specifically functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI), to explore how different regions of the brain communicate. We employ graph theoretical methods to model this intricate neural data with the aim of objective diagnosis of the disorder and identifying neurological markers that could improve the diagnostic process for BPD. To achieve this, we make use of publicly available, annotated task-fMRI datasets designed to differentiate between individuals with BPD and healthy controls (HC). Through rigorous statistical analysis, correlation studies, and the application of graph-based metrics, we aim to not only identify whether an individual is suffering from the disorder or not, but also uncover specific brain regions that exhibit distinct activity patterns in individuals with BPD compared to HC. This research seeks to deepen our comprehension of BPD and potentially enhance diagnostic procedures by acting as an aid to health professionals.

articleTitle: Power Density Prediction in PEM Fuel Cells Using Semi-Supervised and Supervised Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) fuel cells are emerging as a promising technology for clean and efficient energy conversion, offering significant advantages in terms of high efficiency, low emissions, and operational flexibility. In recent years, machine learning (ML) and deep learning algorithms have shown great potential in modeling complex PEM fuel cell systems by capturing intricate patterns and relationships within the data. This study aims to leverage the capabilities of semi-supervised and supervised deep learning algorithms to predict the power density of PEM fuel cells, focusing on a comparative analysis between Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) enhanced with Bayesian Optimization. The standard tests of Nafion 112 membrane dataset from the Data Analytics Laboratory, ECSIM Organization, were utilized in predicting the power density of that fuel cell. The novel implementation of a semi-supervised (GCN) algorithm gave an overall model accuracy of 81%, which was then compared with a traditional supervised (ANN) algorithm that gave an overall accuracy greater than 98%. The high accuracy achieved by the ANN model indicates that deep learning algorithms hold great promise for advancing PEM fuel cell technology. Thus, leveraging these algorithms can achieve more efficient and optimized systems, paving the way for more reliable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Mocap-ARM: A Natural Avatar Motion Rendering System Based on Loose-Fit Sensor Jacket
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: We propose a motion capture and adjustable rendering method(Mocap-ARM) for reliably rendering avatars even if there is noise in the input motion data. Conventional motion capture systems apply sensed motion data to avatars directly. In this case, the avatar action may seem unrealistic when the sensed motion data contains noise data. Whereas, our Mocap-ARM recognizes sensed motion data and renders an avatar using the generated motion data. We generated various motion data using the motion data generative model. Our Mocap-ARM can mix the generated motions using our motion data adjusting method. Therefore, if our recognition system can recognize the input motion data containing lots of noise, the avatar can be drawn with various motion data from the motion data generative model. We verified the validity of the Mocap-ARM through a user study. Users compared the proposed system with the existing 1:1 mapping system in the user study. As a result of the comparison, users preferred the Mocap-ARM system.

articleTitle: Small Tumor-Aware Network for Brain MRI Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Brain tumor segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems for brain cancer detection because accurate tumor size, shape, and location are important for further tumor quantification and classification. However, segmenting small tumors in MRI images is challenging due to the speckle noise, varying tumor shapes and sizes among patients, and the existence of tumor-like image regions. Recently, deep learning-based approaches have achieved great success in biomedical image analysis, but current state-of-the-art approaches achieve poor performance for segmenting small brain tumors. In this paper, we propose a UNet++ model - Small Tumor-Aware Network, to accurately and robustly segment brain tumors. The Unet model with special fine tuning like Learning Rate, Loss Function and Hyperparameter Tuning. We compare proposed model with Base UNet against 3D Slicer segmented tumor. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves the best overall performance and is on par with 3D Slicer manually segmented small tumor which is very tedious and tiresome.

articleTitle: Neural Collaborative Filtering with Pairwise Learning for Implicit Feedback Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Deep neural networks have found wide applications in fields such as natural language processing, language translation, computer vision, and speech recognition, including recommendation systems. Among different types of deep neural networks used in recommendation systems, neural collaborative filtering (2017), which is a multilayer perceptron based recommender system, is widely explored as a general model for user-item interactions. Neural collaborative filtering is generic and can express and generalize matrix factorization under its framework. However, pairwise learning of neural collaborative filtering is less explored. In this paper, we present a framework NCF-PL, short for neural collaborative filtering with pairwise learning to model the pairwise preference of the items for the users using implicit feedback data. To model user-item interaction, both dot product and MLP are explored. Using dot product to model user-item interaction generalizes matrix factorization under the NCF-PL framework. We perform experiments on two real-world datasets to demonstrate the improvements of our NCF-PL framework over the state-of-the-art Bayesian personalized ranking framework.

articleTitle: Maximizing the Prediction Accuracy of Needle Deflection by Random Forest through Bayesian Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Subcutaneous needle insertion has become prevalent in minimally invasive surgery. However, it is expected that thin and elongated needles tends to experience bending due to interaction between the needle and surrounding tissue. Consequently, this bending of needles leads to misalignment of the needle tip, adversely affecting the effectiveness of interventional radiology techniques such as radio frequency ablation of kidney tumors. To improve radiation therapy, robotized needle steering techniques can be one of the solutions. However a precise needle deflection prediction is essential. Therefore, this article introduces a random forest technique to predict the needle deflection. Actualized the gradation of accuracy is challenging due to the dynamic environment inside the human body. The random forest with ensemble learning increases the prediction accuracy by majority voting. The mean absolute error is decreased by 0.5 as compared to decision tree.

articleTitle: Productivity App for ADHD Affected People
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: This project introduces the creation of a productivity application specifically designed to cater to the requirements of individuals impacted by Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). Leveraging machine learning techniques, the application aims to augment emotional intelligence and promote self-reflection by analyzing written text. By identifying and acknowledging their emotions, users can cultivate deeper awareness of their mental conditions, fostering personal development and enhancing productivity.

articleTitle: Global Trends and Research Hotspots in Insurtech: A Bibliometric Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: The financial sector has been feeling the tremors of the digital revolution for some time now. The same trend is occurring within the insurance sector which has seen minimal disruption over an extended period. This study aims to identify current trends in the scholarly literature on the topic of global trends and research hotspots in Insurtech. It was done by applying a bibliometric review of documents published in the Scopus database. We analysed Insurtech-related publications on Scopus based on keywords relevant to Insurtech in the article's titles, keywords and abstract. The focus of this study is mainly on the Co-Authorship Analysis of Countries and the Co-Occurrence Analysis of Keywords based on textual data. In this regard, 394 publications were identified by using the keywords ‘InsurTech AND Natural Language’ OR ‘InsurTech AND Big data’ OR ‘InsurTech AND Artificial Intelligence’ OR ‘InsurTech AND IoT’ OR ‘InsurTech AND Blockchain’ OR ‘InsurTech AND Cloud Computing’ OR ‘InsurTech AND Machine Learning’ OR ‘InsurTech AND Telematics’ OR ‘InsurTech AND Chatbots’ OR ‘InsurTech AND Cybersecurity’ to create the mapping. The study was done by data visualization using the Vos Viewer software application. During the data processing, standard bibliometric indicators like the year of publication, language, document type, source title, source type, study field, keyword analysis, also authorship were used. The date of publications on InsurTech starts from the Scopus database started in 2018 till 2024. The results prove that scientific research about Insurtech has been increasing while there has been considerable attention to the implications of technology in the Insurance sector. Moreover, we analyzed the countries whose authors have advanced InsurTech research. The findings show that Spain leads, followed by Italy, Switzerland, the USA, and India.

articleTitle: Plausible and Effective Gesture-Based Interactions for the Virtual Runway
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: As Virtual Reality and other virtual environment platforms evolve, the need for and research into diverse new input methods as alternatives to traditional keyboard inputs have been highlighted. This study developed a motion recognition-based input method using IMU sensors to track user movements, thereby designing a virtual runway where users can control avatars within a virtual environment. Additionally, we defined flight movements for human avatars in virtual environments and trained a motion generation network using a preprocessed dataset to enable the generation of these flight movements. User motions were recognized through the measurement of joint angles and permissible ranges. To assess the usability and user experience of this innovative approach, a usability test was conducted that compared the gesture-based input method to traditional keyboard input under various experimental conditions. The results demonstrated that the gesture-based input method had a lower error rate than keyboard input. Furthermore, the gesture-based input method outperformed keyboard input in the hedonic quality of the User Experience Questionnaire: attractiveness, simulation, and novelty.

articleTitle: Completing the Puzzle: Knowledge Graph Augmentation Using GANs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) play a crucial role in information management and artificial intelligence connecting complex webs of data, enabling inference and decision-making. However, there is a big problem with KGs: they are incomplete. The proposed study intends to complete Knowledge Graphs by creating vector embeddings for PICKLE and FB15k-237 datasets, identifying sparsity in the generated knowledge graphs using Gini index and node density metrics, generating missing nodes using GANs and embedding the generated nodes along with links in the parent KG. Integration of synthetic nodes and links using Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) further enrich the KG, ensuring proper alignment with existing structures. RotatE outperforms other Vector Embedding Models in terms of metrics such as Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) and Hits@k.

articleTitle: Multi-object Tracking using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Multi-object Tracking (MOT) is a technique to identify or detect and track objects in images and videos. We introduce a deep learning model with just one complex neural network. The method, detection by tracking uses a detector called SSD (Single Shot Detector) a deep learning network which is trained and evaluated on the Pascal VOC (2007+2012) dataset based on 20 different object classes which has over 16k images used for training and over 4k images used for evaluation of the detection model. SSD discretizes the outcome area by creating prior boxes having varying aspect ratios and scales of feature maps and arranging them into bounding boxes for every position. Moreover, the detection output integrates with the tracker from various feature maps with varying resolutions to effectively manage and track the moving objects of different dimensions in a video. Results from experimentation are conducted on the PASCAL VOOC2007 test dataset, SSD attains a 73% mAP for input frame of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$300\times 300$</tex>. The accuracy is similar to progressive model. In comparison, the performance is further enhanced with the addition of tracker to other single stage techniques.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning for Cricket Shot Classification: An Inception-v3 Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Deep learning finds its application in multiple disciplines from healthcare to security systems. Convolution neural networks a part of deep learning architecture power the computers with human visionary capabilities. Its application in the sports industry has changed the landscape of coaching by providing real-time analysis of player shots and helping prevent players from getting injured based on pose estimation techniques. Cricket is one of the most popular games across the world that involves immense concentration and hand-eye coordination skills to excel in the game. The integration of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with cricket has evolved the game to the next level in recent years. In this work, we build a CNN model using transfer learning methods to classify four different batting shots based on their specific movements. We used the popular Kaggle cricket shots dataset which consists of 4723 images that belong to any of the four batting shots. Inception-v3, a pretrained convolutional neural network model that was trained on the ImageNet dataset was utilized because of its deep neural network capabilities while efficiently using computational resources. Once after training the model using different sets of hyperparameters, our model achieved an accuracy of 98.7% on the provided test dataset and showed impressive results in other performance metrics as well.

articleTitle: Enhancing Bharatanatyam Face Emotion Recognition Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Facial Expression Analysis of Bharatanatyam a Classical South Indian Dance Using Machine Learning Techniques The research explores how emotion alters facial expressions, particularly the areas of expression in the eyebrows and surrounding structures, lips, and mouth region. Local binary patterns (LBP), grey-level cooccurrence matrix (GLCM), Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) and invariants descriptors such as Discrete cosine transforms (DCT) or oriented fast and rotated brief (ORB). Finally, using SVM (Support Vector Machine), KNN (K-Nearest Neighbours), DT (Decision Tree), and RF (Random Forest) classifiers the deafest features are tested separately. Experiments are carried out via a Bharatanatyam face image database, and it is inferred that the combination of DCT with RF gives the best performance in classification. From the evaluations for colour-scale and grey-scale images, we can see that DCT with RF has an accuracy of 82.14%, and 80.40% is colour scale and greyscale respectively According to the above results, it is concluded that DCT along with RF has successfully categorized emotional facial expression of Bharatanatyam.

articleTitle: Leveraging AI in Anti Money Laundering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Money laundering has become a prevalent method for organizations to avoid taxes, fund terrorist activities, and engage in various illegal practices, posing a significant threat to the integrity and security of global financial institutions. Traditional rule-based systems often fail to detect new patterns of money laundering, leading to non-compliance, increasingly outdated, industry inefficient and generate a high number of false positives. This study explores current practices in fraud risk management by financial institutions and leveraging AI in the field of AML by training machine learning models to improve the accuracy in detecting suspicious transactions and reducing false positives. The proposed model training process encompasses several steps, including cleaning and preparing the dataset, augmenting the dataset to increase the examples of anomalies,and building time series models to detect the fraudulent transactions with respect to time according to RBA. Additionally other ML algorithms for anomaly detection have been implemented for improvement in accuracy than traditional RBA. An autoencoder model is deployed to reduce the dimensionality in the dataset. Further the encoded dataset is used on the same ML algorithms for anomaly detection to examine the improvement in the accuracy.

articleTitle: Comparing the Adaptability of a Genetic Algorithm and an LLM-Based Framework for Automated Software Test Data Generation: In the Context of Web Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: In the fast-paced world of software development, ensuring software quality is paramount. Software Quality Assurance (SQA) plays a vital role, primarily through testing, which can be carried out manually or automatically. Yet, creating comprehensive test data (TD) for web applications can be a formidable task. Manual test data generation (TDG) is time-consuming and error prone. Automation of TDG has become increasingly important in the realm of software quality assurance as it enables efficient and effective testing of software systems. The need for an appropriate framework for automated TDG is critical to achieve comprehensive and reliable test coverage. Automated TDG offers significant advantages, including time and resource savings, improved test coverage, and seamless integration into the software development process. The core aim of this research is to bridge the gap between manual and existing automated methods, resulting in time and cost savings, heightened testing efficiency, and elevated software quality. Research objectives encompass comparing the adaptability of an AGA based automated TDG model and a LLM based automated TDG model to a web application. The results from the LLM model for triangle classification program was found to be potentially acceptable and accurate than the AGA model's results. This research discusses the challenges encountered when implementing and using the AGA-based framework in the web application context and how an LLM model could overcome the challenges. The study highlights the benefits of using the LLM approach, demonstrating its relevance and accuracy in generating test data compared to the Genetic Algorithm-based model. The practical implications for software quality assurance practices are discussed, emphasizing the enhanced efficiency and effectiveness of the LLM model in improving software quality.

articleTitle: Misinformation Detection Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Model with Transformer Based Pre-Trained ALBERT Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: Rise of social media platforms has made the spread of information easier. This also raises the issue of spreading misinformation which creates serious problems for society and governments and has a negative impact on many facets of daily life. One of the difficult problems in natural language processing is misinformation detection, which involves separating misinformation from genuine (or truthful) information. This study proposes a transformer-based pretrained Albert model and integrated deep learning model which provides enhanced feature learning on dataset collected from different sources to provide a solution to the problem of misinformation detection. The dataset used for the task is a combination of Liar, genuine and misleading information which leads to Combined Corpus dataset. The deep learning model used are Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Unit (Bi-GRU) and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to provide better feature engineering to categorize genuine and misinformation. A base Albert model has also been trained on the Combined Corpus (CC) dataset to evaluate the effect of enhanced feature learning using Bi-GRU and CNN with Albert. The results obtained reflect 1.30% and 0.76% increment in accuracy on Combined Corpus (CC) dataset from the base Albert model.

articleTitle: Secured File Transmission for Printing Using Wi-Fi
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
abstract: The most popular method of printing documents is through WhatsApp file sharing or document sharing. Recently, there has been no security around the transmission of private information or papers via WhatsApp, which could cause a lot of trouble because the user must make sure the shopkeeper has received and printed the right document. It can occasionally result in the contact numbers being misused as well. Conversely, the network problems encountered when sending the documents result from more users sharing the file at once and, occasionally, from poor network coverage, which makes sharing the file take longer and inconvenient for both the sender and the recipient, making the next user wait. I suggested the problem statement that can be used to resolve this issue. “PrintEnd”, a mobile application is a comprehensive solution for managing documents, data, and workflows in a streamlined and efficient manner. This innovative app brings together a range of tools and technologies to enable organizations to digitize their operations, enhance collaboration, and optimize productivity. With a user-friendly interface and advanced features such as automated document capture, intelligent routing, and secure cloud storage, the PrintEnd simplifies complex processes and empowers employees to work smarter and faster. An application is made so that users can easily provide the necessary papers in accordance with the specifications. The documents are sent to the receiver end, where they are received and printed by the shopkeeper. Wi-Fi file transfer is the key concept used to build the problem statement.
